course_name_en: Software Architecture: Concepts and Practical Implementations
prerequisites: Good knowledge of programming paradigms and advanced knowledge of object-oriented programming concepts.
Very good knowledge of an object-oriented programming language.
Basic knowledge of requirements analysis, software design, and the development of distributed systems.
Good prior knowledge of databases and their use.

learning_outcomes.text: Students can distinguish and describe fundamental principles, styles, and patterns of software architecture.
Students can define the requirements relevant for software architecture.
Students can design a software architecture based on the requirements for a defined software architecture style.
Students can apply selected technologies for the implementation of a software architecture design.
Students can identify and design the fundamental structure of complex software.
Students can define interfaces of high-level software components and their forms of interaction.
Students can characterize quality attributes such as maintainability, correctness, security, and availability, and consider them in design and implementation.
Students can create integration and automated system tests.
Students can design a software architecture and critically evaluate decisions based on their expert knowledge.
Students can verify and prove the viability of the software architecture.
Students can design software architectures for defined software architecture styles.
Students know technologies for implementing and testing software architecture.
Students can apply and evaluate established procedures and methods for designing a software architecture.
Students can discuss software architecture designs with subject matter experts and non-experts with theoretically and methodologically sound argumentation and develop solutions.
Students can use established procedures and methods for designing a software architecture.

assessment_methods.method: Written exam or presentation (with written elaboration) or project report (written)

assessment_rules: The selection of graded and ungraded examination types from the given options is at the discretion of the respective lecturer, adhering to the valid study regulations. The ungraded proof of performance is provided as part of the accompanying internship. The examination forms for the graded examination are a) written exam, b) presentation (with written elaboration), or c) project report (written) as described in the valid study regulations. For regular attendance, a minimum of 80% attendance is required.
